speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilic Arthropathy secondary to undiagnosed Hemophilia A or B. Given the patient's age (18 months), spontaneous swelling after minor activity (playing in the park), absence of trauma, and the maternal uncle's history of similar problems, this presentation is highly suggestive of a bleeding disorder. The joint swelling likely results from repeated micro-hemorrhages.

REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Profile (PT, PTT), Factor VIII and Factor IX levels.
REQUEST IMAGES: Right Knee X-Ray to check for early signs of hemophilic arthropathy (such as subchondral cysts or erosions).
